source_text: αὐτόν, καὶ μόνον εἰδὸς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἐπὶ πάντας τυγχάνον, λέγουσι τοιάδε· 2.2 Μωυσὴς μὲν ἐν τῇ γενέσει ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ θεοῦ· «οὐ μὴ καταμείνῃ τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τούτοις εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτοὺς σάρκας». Ἀγγαῖος ὁμοίως ἀπὸ θεϊκῆς φωνῆς· «ἐγώ εἰμι μεθ' ὑμῶν, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐφέστηκεν ἐν μέσῳ ὑμῶν·» 2.3 Ζαχαρίας ὁμοίως· «πλὴν ἀκούσατε τοὺς λόγους μου, καὶ τὰ νόμιμά μου δέχεσθε, ἃ ἐγὼ ἐντέλλομαι ἐν πνεύματί μου τοῖς δούλοις μου τοῖς προφήταις·» 2.4 Ἠσαίας ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς τὸν υἱόν· «πνεῦμα τὸ ἐμόν, ὅ ἐστιν ἐπὶ σοί, καὶ τὰ ῥήματα, ἃ δέδωκα εἰς τὸ στόμα σου, οὐ μὴ ἐκλείπῃ ἐκ τοῦ στόματός σου καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ σπέρματός σου·» σπέρμα λέγων αὐτοῦ τοὺς πιστούς, οὓς καὶ εἰς υἱοθεσίαν ἐκάλεσεν. 2.5 καὶ πάλιν ἀπὸ τοῦ υἱοῦ· «πνεῦμα κυρίου ἐπ' ἐμέ.» ἐκπεπεράνθαι σὲ ταῦτα ἐν τῇ οἰκονομίᾳ Ματθαῖος οὕτως εἶπεν· «ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαίου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· "4ἰδοὺ ὁ παῖς μου, ὃν ᾑρέτισα, ὁ ἀγαπητός μου, εἰς ὃν εὐ δόκησεν ἡ ψυχή μου· θήσω τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐπ' αὐτόν·"5» 2.6 καὶ πάλιν ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρός· «πνεῦμα γὰρ ἐξ ἐμοῦ ἐξελεύσεται.» 2.7 καὶ ἐν τῷ Ἰεζεκιὴλ ὁ ὕψιστος πατὴρ τὸ μὲν ἡμέτερον πνεῦμα «ὑμῶν» πνεῦμα, τὸ δὲ ἅγιον πνεῦμα ἴδιον ἐξονομάζει, ἅτε ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἐκπορευθὲν κατὰ φύσιν· «καὶ δώσω ὑμῖν καρδίαν καινὴν 43 καὶ πνεῦμα καινόν· καὶ ἀφελῶ τὴν καρδίαν τὴν λιθίνην ἐκ τῆς σαρκὸς ὑμῶν, καὶ δώσω ὑμῖν καρδίαν σαρκίνην, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμά μου δώσω ἐν ὑμῖν·» 2.8 καὶ ἐν τῷ Ἰωήλ· «ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματός μου ἐπὶ πᾶσαν σάρκα·» 2.9 καὶ ταῦτα τετελέσθαι Παῦλος ἔγραψεν Τίτῳ· «ὅτε ἐπεφάνη ἡ χάρις ἡ σωτήριος ἡμῶν, οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων, ὧν ἐποιήσαμεν ἡμεῖς, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸ πολὺ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος ἀνα γεννήσας ἡμᾶς διὰ λουτροῦ παλιγγενεσίας καὶ ἀνακαινώ σεως πνεύματος ἁγίου, οὗ ἐξέχεεν ἐφ' ἡμᾶς πλουσίως διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.» 2.10 πότε δὲ ἐξέχεεν; ὅτε ὁ Χριστὸς ἐμφυσῶν ἔλεγεν· «λάβετε πνεῦμα ἅγιον,» εὖ δὲ καὶ τὸ «ἐξέχεεν», ἅτε ὕδωρ ἐξ αὐτοῦ ὁμοουσίως ἐκπορευθὲν καὶ μύρον θεϊκόν, καθὰ εὐκαίρως ἐν τοῖς ἁρμόζουσιν τόποις δειχθήσεται πρὸς ἡμῶν· 2.11 καὶ τὸ «ἐπὶ πᾶσαν σάρκα.» αἱ γὰρ λέξεις αὗται ἐπὶ τῆς ἐν ὁμάδι μεθεκτῆς οὐσίας τῆς ἁγίας τριάδος ἁρμόζουσιν, ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐπὶ κτιστῆς ἀμεθέκτου λογικῆς φύσεως· οὐ γάρ που ἐγράφη οὔτε λέγειν πιθανόν· «ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀρχαγγέλου», ἀλλ' ἀπὸ πνεύματός μου, καὶ οὐδὲ οὕτως ἀπολελυμένως, ἀλλ'· «ἐπὶ πᾶσαν σάρκα». 2.12 καὶ ∆αυὶδ δὲ ἱκετεύων βοᾶ· «τὸ πνεῦμά σου τὸ ἅγιον μὴ ἀντανέλῃς ἀπ' ἐμοῦ» καὶ πάλιν· «τὸ πνεῦμά σου τὸ ἅγιον ὁδηγήσει με ἐν γῇ εὐθείᾳ.» καὶ Ματθαῖος ἀπὸ τοῦ υἱοῦ· «οὐ ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ λαλοῦντες, ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ πατρός μου τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν ὑμῖν», ὅ ἐστιν· οὐχ ὑμεῖς οἱ κτιστοί, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἄκτιστον πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ. 2.13 γράφει δὲ καὶ Παῦλος πρὸς μὲν Κορινθίους ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ ἐπιστολῇ· «ἃ ὀφθαλμὸς οὐκ εἶδεν, καὶ οὖς οὐκ ἤκουσεν, καὶ ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἀνέβη· ἃ ἡτοίμασεν ὁ θεὸς τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν, ἡμῖν δὲ ἀπεκάλυψεν ὁ θεὸς διὰ τοῦ πνεύ ματος αὐτοῦ. τὸ πνεῦμα πάντα ἐρευνᾷ καὶ τὰ βάθη τοῦ θεοῦ. τίς γὰρ οἶδεν ἀνθρώπων τὰ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, εἰ μὴ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ; οὕτω καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐδεὶς οἶδεν, εἰ μὴ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ. ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐ πνεῦμα τοῦ κόσμου ἐλάβομεν, ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ· ἵνα ἴδωμεν τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ χαρισθέντα ἡμῖν.» 2.14 τὰ «ἡτοιμασμένα» παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀγαθὰ εἶπεν, ὅτι «τὸ πνεῦμα» «ἀπεκάλυψεν» ὡς συνδοτήρ· καὶ «τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ» κατὰ ἀντιπαράθεσιν τοῦ ἡμετέρου πνεύματος. καὶ ἐπασφαλιζόμενος αὖθις τὸ μὴ νομίζεσθαι αὐτὸ ὡς ἄγγελον ἢ ἄλλο πνεῦμα κτιστόν, ἐπήγαγεν· «οὐ πνεῦμα τοῦ κόσμου ἐλάβομεν»–τουτέστιν γενητόν–»ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ»–τουτέστιν ἐξ ὑπολειπομένων, τὸ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς ὑποστάσεως ἐκπορευθέν· καὶ ὡς αὐτὸ μόνον οἶδεν τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὡς κύριος, καὶ ἔχον ὡσαύτως τῇ φύσει πρὸς τὸν πατέρα. ὁ γάρ· «δοῦλος», –ὡς ἐν εὐαγγελίῳ λέγει, –»οὐκ οἶδεν τί ποιεῖ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ.» 2.15 οὐκέτι δὲ ὡς ἐπὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἶπεν τὸ κατοικοῦν «ἐν τῷ θεῷ», ἵνα μὴ σύνθετος νομισθείῃ ὁ ἀσύνθετος θεός. 2.16 πρὸς δὲ Ἐφεσίους· «μὴ λυπεῖτε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐν ᾧ ἐσφρα γίσθητε εἰς ἡμέραν ἀναπολυτρώσεως»· 2.17 πρὸς δὲ Ῥωμαίους· «ὑμεῖς οὔκ ἐστε ἐν σαρκί, ἀλλ' ἐν πνεύματι, εἴπερ πνεῦμα θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν· εἰ δέ τις πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ οὐκ ἔχει, οὗτος οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ»· 2.18 πρὸς δὲ Γαλάτας· «ὅτι δέ ἐστε υἱοί, ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ θεὸς τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν, κράζον ἀββᾶ ὁ πατήρ»· 2.19 πρὸς δὲ Φιλιππησίους· pass_a_gloss: [... after] him, and that alone it knows the things of God, and comes to be upon all, they say such things: 2.2 Moses in Genesis, from the person of God: 'my spirit shall by no means remain in these men into the age, because of their being flesh'. Haggai likewise from a divine voice: 'I am with you, and my spirit has stood in the midst of you'; 2.3 Zechariah likewise: 'but hear my words, and receive my statutes, which I command in my spirit to my slaves the prophets'; 2.4 Isaiah, from the Father to the Son: 'my spirit, which is upon you, and the words which I have given into your mouth, shall by no means fail from your mouth and from the mouth of your seed', calling his seed the faithful, whom he also called into adoption as sons. 2.5 And again from the Son: 'the spirit of the Lord upon me'. That these things have been carried to completion in the economy Matthew said thus: 'so that the thing spoken through Isaiah the prophet be fulfilled, saying: behold my servant, whom I chose, my beloved, in whom my soul was well pleased; I will put my spirit upon him'. 2.6 And again from the Father: 'for a spirit will go out from me'. 2.7 And in Ezekiel the highest Father names our spirit 'your' spirit, but names the Holy Spirit his own, as having proceeded from him by nature: 'and I will give you a new heart and a new spirit; and I will take away the stone heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a fleshly heart, and I will give my spirit in you'; 2.8 and in Joel: 'I will pour out from my spirit upon all flesh'; 2.9 and that these things have been completed Paul wrote to Titus: 'when the saving grace of ours appeared, not out of works which we ourselves did, but according to his much mercy, having begotten us again through a bath of rebirth and renewal of Holy Spirit, which he poured out upon us richly through Jesus Christ'. 2.10 And when did he pour out? When Christ, breathing in, was saying: 'receive Holy Spirit'. And well also the 'poured out', as having proceeded from him consubstantially as water, and [as] divine ointment, just as will be shown by us opportunely in the fitting places; 2.11 and the 'upon all flesh'. For these expressions fit the essence of the holy Trinity that is shared in together by a company, but not a created rational nature that is not shared in; for nowhere was it written, nor is it plausible to say: 'I will pour out from the archangel', but from my spirit, and not even thus absolutely, but: 'upon all flesh'. 2.12 And David too, supplicating, cries: 'your holy spirit do not take away from me', and again: 'your holy spirit will guide me on level land'. And Matthew from the Son: 'it is not you who are the ones speaking, but the spirit of my Father, the one speaking in you', which is: not you the created ones, but the uncreated spirit of God. 2.13 And Paul also writes to the Corinthians in the first letter: 'things which eye did not see and ear did not hear and did not go up upon a heart of man, things which God prepared for those loving him, but to us God revealed through his spirit. The spirit searches all things, even the depths of God. For who of men knows the things of the man, except the spirit of the man that is in him? So also the things of God no one knows, except the spirit of God. But we did not receive the spirit of the world, but the spirit that is from God, so that we may see the things graciously given to us by God'. 2.14 He spoke of the good things 'prepared' by God, that 'the spirit' 'revealed' [them] as co-giver; and 'his spirit' by contrast with our spirit. And making secure again that it not be thought of as an angel or another created spirit, he brought on: 'we did not receive the spirit of the world' — that is, a thing come into being — 'but the spirit that is from God' — that is, from the remaining [alternative], the one having proceeded from the hypostasis of God; and how it alone knows the things of God, as Lord, and holding likewise by nature toward the Father. For the 'slave', as he says in the gospel, 'does not know what his lord does'. 2.15 But he no longer said, as in the case of the man, the thing dwelling 'in God', so that the uncompounded God not be thought compounded. 2.16 And to the Ephesians: 'do not grieve the holy spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for a day of redemption'; 2.17 and to the Romans: 'you are not in flesh but in spirit, if indeed spirit of God dwells in you; but if anyone does not have spirit of Christ, this one is not his'; 2.18 and to the Galatians: 'and that you are sons, God sent out the spirit of his son into your hearts, crying abba the Father'; 2.19 and to the Philippians: 'for I know that [...]'
pass_b_english: … him, and that he alone knows the things of God and comes upon all, they say such things as these.

Moses in Genesis, speaking in the person of God: “My spirit shall not remain in these men for ever, because they are flesh” (Genesis 6:3). Haggai likewise, with the divine voice: “I am with you, and my spirit stands in your midst” (Haggai 2:4-5). Zechariah likewise: “But hear my words, and receive my statutes, which I command by my spirit to my servants the prophets” (Zechariah 1:6).

Isaiah, speaking from the Father to the Son: “My spirit, which is upon you, and the words which I have put in your mouth, shall not fail from your mouth or from the mouth of your seed” (Isaiah 59:21). By his seed he means the faithful, whom he also called to adoption as sons. And again, in the person of the Son: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me” (Isaiah 61:1). That these things were brought to fulfilment in the economy of salvation Matthew stated thus: “So that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which says: Behold my servant, whom I have chosen, my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased; I will put my spirit upon him” (Matthew 12:17-18). And again, in the person of the Father: “For a spirit shall go forth from me” (Isaiah 57:16 LXX).

And in Ezekiel the Most High Father calls our spirit “your” spirit, but names the Holy Spirit his own, since it proceeded from him by nature: “And I will give you a new heart and a new spirit; and I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh and give you a heart of flesh; and I will put my spirit within you” (Ezekiel 36:26-27). And in Joel: “I will pour out of my spirit upon all flesh” (Joel 2:28).

And that these things have been accomplished Paul wrote to Titus: “When our saving grace appeared, not by works that we ourselves had done, but according to his great mercy, he gave us new birth through the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit, whom he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ” (Titus 3:4-6).

And when did he pour him out? When Christ breathed on them and said, “Receive the Holy Spirit” (John 20:22). “Poured out” is well said, too, since the Spirit proceeded from him consubstantially, like water, and is a divine ointment, as we will show at the right time in the places that suit it. And so is “upon all flesh”. For these words fit the essence of the Holy Trinity, which is shared by many together, and not a created rational nature, which cannot be shared. For nowhere was it written, nor would it be plausible to say, “I will pour out of the archangel”; but “of my spirit”, and not even that without qualification, but “upon all flesh”.

And David, too, cries out in supplication: “Do not take your holy spirit from me” (Psalm 51:11); and again: “Your holy spirit will guide me on level ground” (Psalm 143:10). And Matthew, quoting the Son: “It is not you who speak, but the Spirit of my Father who speaks in you” (Matthew 10:20); that is, not you, who are created, but the uncreated Spirit of God.

Paul, too, writes to the Corinthians in his first letter: “What eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and has not entered the heart of man, what God has prepared for those who love him, God has revealed to us through his Spirit. For the Spirit searches all things, even the depths of God. For who among men knows the things of a man, except the spirit of the man that is in him? So also no one knows the things of God, except the Spirit of God. Now we have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may know the things freely given us by God” (1 Corinthians 2:9-12).

He spoke of the good things “prepared” by God, and said that “the Spirit” “revealed” them, as one who gives together with God; and he said “his Spirit” in contrast to our spirit. And taking care once more that the Spirit should not be thought an angel or some other created spirit, he added: “We have not received the spirit of the world”, that is, one that came into being, “but the Spirit who is from God”, that is, by elimination, the one who proceeded from the hypostasis of God. And he showed that the Spirit alone knows the things of God, as Lord, and as being the same in nature with the Father. For “the servant”, as he says in the Gospel, “does not know what his master is doing” (John 15:15).
But he did not go on to say, as he did of man, “that dwells in God”, lest the God who is not composite be thought composite.

To the Ephesians: “Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption” (Ephesians 4:30). To the Romans: “You are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you; but if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to him” (Romans 8:9). To the Galatians: “And because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father” (Galatians 4:6). To the Philippians: “For I know that …” (Philippians 1:19)

choices.issue: Old draft garbled, numbered and unreferenced
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English printed edition numbers 2.2 through 2.11 in the reading text, left an empty paragraph '...' between 2.11 and the end of that sentence, gave no references for 2.2-2.11, began 'They say that He, knowing only the things of God … is such', rendered ᾑρέτισα (I chose) as 'whom I have loved', ὁμοουσίως (consubstantially) as 'similarly', συνδοτήρ (co-giver) as 'companion', ἐξ ὑπολειπομένων (by elimination) as 'from the remaining [essence]' with a bracket filler, and turned 2.15 into 'he did not speak as if regarding the man who dwells in God, so that the uncomposed God might be thought composite', the reverse of the sense. References added: Genesis 6:3, Haggai 2:4-5, Zechariah 1:6, Isaiah 59:21, Isaiah 61:1, Matthew 12:17-18, Isaiah 57:16 LXX, Ezekiel 36:26-27, Joel 2:28, Titus 3:4-6, John 20:22, Philippians 1:19. Kept: Psalm 51:11, Psalm 143:10, Matthew 10:20, 1 Corinthians 2:9-12, John 15:15, Ephesians 4:30, Romans 8:9, Galatians 4:6.

choices.term: αὐτόν, καὶ μόνον εἰδὸς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ
choices.english: … him, and that he alone knows the things of God
choices.why: The section opens with the object of μετ' at the end of the previous section ('though not after'); only this section's words are translated, with a leading ellipsis.
Anticipates the argument of 2.8-2.11 from 'I will pour out of my spirit upon all flesh'.

choices.term: ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ θεοῦ / ἀπὸ τοῦ υἱοῦ / ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρός
choices.english: speaking in the person of God / in the person of the Son / of the Father
choices.why: Didymus' formula for the speaker of a prophetic text.

choices.english: That these things were brought to fulfilment
choices.why: σὲ ('you') makes no sense; read as δέ. Recorded under problems.
Technical term for the incarnate work of Christ; 'of salvation' added so the reader does not take it as finance.
Didymus' wording where the New Testament text reads ἔσωσεν (he saved); his participle is translated as he quotes it.

choices.term: ἅτε ὕδωρ ἐξ αὐτοῦ ὁμοουσίως ἐκπορευθὲν καὶ μύρον θεϊκόν
choices.english: since the Spirit proceeded from him consubstantially, like water, and is a divine ointment
choices.why: Images of the Spirit poured out (water, ointment) that Didymus promises to treat later; 'consubstantially' keeps ὁμοουσίως.

choices.term: ἐν ὁμάδι μεθεκτῆς οὐσίας … κτιστῆς ἀμεθέκτου λογικῆς φύσεως
choices.english: the essence of the Holy Trinity, which is shared by many together, and not a created rational nature, which cannot be shared
choices.why: The contrast is between a divine essence that many can share at once and a created spirit (an archangel) that cannot be poured into others.
Logical formula: once 'the spirit of the world' is excluded, what remains is the Spirit from God. No bracketed noun is needed.

choices.term: ἔχον ὡσαύτως τῇ φύσει πρὸς τὸν πατέρα
choices.english: as being the same in nature with the Father
choices.why: ὡσαύτως ἔχειν πρός: to be in the same condition as; the subject is the Spirit.

choices.term: οὐκέτι δὲ ὡς ἐπὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἶπεν τὸ κατοικοῦν «ἐν τῷ θεῷ»
choices.english: But he did not go on to say, as he did of man, “that dwells in God”
choices.why: Paul wrote 'the spirit of the man that is in him' but not 'the Spirit that is in God'; Didymus says he avoided it so God would not seem composite.
The digits 4 and 5 inside the Matthew quotation are footnote markers in the copy-text; skipped.
'43' is a printed page number in the copy-text; skipped. Split words (εὐ δόκησεν, ἀνα γεννήσας, ἀνακαινώ σεως, πνεύ ματος, ἐσφρα γίσθητε) read as single words.
The section ends mid-quotation; the next section completes Philippians 1:19.
